newsitem.title: MONACO: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER GOES TOP WITH MONACO WIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SCHUMACHER GOES TOP WITH MONACO WIN.

text.p: Twice world champion Michael Schumacher showed that Ferrari can be a potent force in this year's world drivers' championship by taking the lead on Sunday with a masterful victory in the Monaco Grand Prix.

The 28-year-old German led in his Ferrari from start to finish in a race cut from 78 laps to two hours, after only 62 laps, because of the weather which, as in 1996, reduced the field to only a handful of runners at the finish.

Schumacher's third win in four years on the famous Mediterranean street circuit lifted him to 24 points in the drivers standings, four clear of Canadian Jacques Villeneuve who was one of the 12 non-finishers in his Williams.
Schumacher's first win this season put him ahead for the first time since he left Benetton to join Ferrari after winning the 1995 world title.
But he refused to be drawn on his prospects of a third championship.

"There are 12 races to go and we have a very difficult race ahead of us at Barcelona next," he said, after confirming he had swapped his race car, set for dry conditions, before the start to a spare car set up for wet.

The result was that Schumacher romped home 53 seconds clear of Brazilian Rubens Barrichello, whose fine drive earned the Stewart team their first points. Briton Eddie Irvine in the second Ferrari was third ahead of last year's winner, Frenchman Olivier Panis, in a Prost.
It was Irvine's third successive podium finish and those three were the only drivers not lapped by Schumacher.
Mika Salo of Finland, driving a Tyrrell, was fifth with Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan sixth.

Schumacher's win also ended Ferrari's long wait since their last victory in Monaco by Gilles Villeneuve in 1981. It also helped them celebrate the 50th anniversary this month of the founding of the team by Enzo Ferrari.
Schumacher said: "It was a very tricky race and in some of the corners I had to go so slow that I thought I could get out and run faster than the car, but it was the same for everyone.
"We had two possible options with the cars and I chose the one for the wet. It was right for me, but I still had lots of moments. A very difficult race, but a good one."

It was a disastrous race for the Williams team. Previous leader Villeneuve and team-mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany, who started from pole position, both failed to finish after selecting 'slick' dry weather tyres and set-ups for the start of the race.
The McLaren and Benetton teams also suffered in the conditions, only Austrian Gerhard Berger in a Benetton finishing out of their four cars on a day when the weather played havoc with plans.
Schumacher was simply at his brilliant best and, apart from one 'moment' after 52 laps when he missed his braking point and ran straight on at the Sainte Devote corner, he drove a faultless race.
He took control from the start and was 6.6 seconds ahead after the first lap, 28 ahead after 10 and in the distance from then on.
Fisichella was in contention early but fell away and Barrichello, who started 10th, and Irvine, 15th on the grid, made steady progress to join him on the podium.
Schumacher's younger brother Ralf, 21, in the second Jordan, was among the early front-runners but after running third and then fourth he crashed out in Casino Square.

Villeneuve was never in contention and said: "We had data telling us it would dry after 20 or 30 minutes so we decided to keep the dry set-up and the slicks, but it started to rain more so they were useless. Eventually, I hit the guard rail and the car was too damaged to carry on."
Barrichello said he was delighted for the new Stewart team because they have worked so hard to become competitive this year in such a short time.

"It is a really great day for me and for the team," he said. "It is not that long ago I remember getting up in Brazil and watching this race on television -- and my ambition this morning was just to finish."
Irvine said he had accidents galore, hitting cars at the front, side and rear, and praised the strength of his Ferrari for his survival.
"It was really chaotic," he said, after joining Schumacher in hoisting team chief Jean Todt on their shoulders in celebration at the end of the race.
